None of these were implemented. They are out of scope for the repair, which was limited to

`requirements.md` specifies only `native` and `external`. Every other owner falls through to a

fallback in `requirements.md`, or raise `ValueError` on an unrecognised owner so typos surface
instead of silently returning a plausible-looking status.

`"platform-pending"`, `"verified"` and `"bound"` are untyped literals duplicated across code and
tests. An `enum.Enum` (or module-level constants) would make a typo a failure at import time
rather than a silent wrong answer.

`backlog.md` states "Previous contract: native workspaces return verified" with nothing pointing

assertion look plausible. Suggest annotating it as superseded and dating it. (Left unchanged
here, as instructed.)

`README.md` says to validate with `python3 -c 'import json; json.load(open("diagnosis.json"))'`,
whereas the assignment requires `python3 -m json.tool diagnosis.json`. Two documented
validation paths for the same artifact will keep diverging; pick one and record it in `README.md`.

Nothing in the suite would catch a future edit that reintroduces the old contract. A test
asserting the full `native`/`external` mapping in one place — rather than two independent
assertions — would make the contract legible as a unit.

## 6. Test suite has no failure-path or parametrised coverage
`test_lifecycle.py` is two hard-coded equality checks. A table-driven test over
`(owner, expected)` pairs would make adding a third owner a one-line change.
